about: The Catalyst word list (rule 8.43). Terms are settled; a definition with "confirmed": false is a draft waiting for a product owner pass (BACKLOG). A term's definition doubles as its hint-tooltip text (rule 8.49).

settings.name: entity name
settings.notes: An organisation may rename "investment" to "project"; copy takes the name from the setting.

terms.definition: A piece of work that competes for funding, with one or more alternatives.
terms.notes: An organisation may rename it "project" (USER-SETTINGS row 15): copy takes the entity name from the setting and never hard-codes "investment" or "project". "Project" is not a banned word.

terms.definition: An investment type that groups related work.
terms.notes: A real investment type (decided Nov 26), not a level of portfolio. Whether an organisation may rename it is in the backlog.

terms.definition: One way to carry out an investment, with its own cost, timing and value.
terms.notes: Distinct from scenario (a whole plan). "Option" stays fine for menu and radio choices, never for an alternative.

terms.definition: The alternative the plan currently uses for an investment.
terms.notes: One number per investment = the selected alternative.

terms.definition: One version of the portfolio plan, under its own constraints and assumptions.
terms.notes: Names as entered ("02_Optimized").

terms.definition: A group of investments planned and funded together. Portfolios can contain other portfolios.
terms.notes: "Program" is an investment type, not a portfolio (decided Nov 26), so it is no longer on this list.

terms.definition: A set of investments in a scenario that the optimization treats the same way.
A score from the value framework, not money. Higher is better.
terms.notes: Never with a currency symbol; K / M allowed ("Value 15.85M", rules 8.26, 8.43).

terms.definition: Your organization's model for measuring the value of investments against its goals.
A calculation in a value framework that scores investments on one measure.
One thing the value framework measures, such as reliability risk or aggregate risk.
terms.notes: Measure names as entered ("Reliability-Risk").

terms.definition: A limit the optimization must respect, such as a yearly capex cap.
terms.notes: The umbrella word: "14 constraints". A spend limit is a budget.

terms.definition: A constraint that limits spend, such as the FY27 budget.
terms.notes: One kind of constraint (decided Nov 26): "budget" for a spend limit, "constraint" as the umbrella; never "budget" for value or other limits.

terms.definition: A run that picks alternatives and timing to get the most value within the constraints.
terms.notes: US spelling. Verb "optimize", adjective "optimized"; re-optimize is hyphenated (rule 8.42).

terms.definition: Status: the investment starts later than requested.
terms.notes: Optimizer status.

terms.definition: Status: the investment starts earlier than requested.
terms.notes: Optimizer status.

terms.definition: Status: the plan uses a different alternative than requested.
terms.notes: Optimizer status.

terms.definition: Status: no change from the request.
terms.notes: "Requested" is the scenario name.

terms.definition: The planned spend of an alternative by year.
Capital and operating expenditure.
terms.notes: "capex" in running text, "Capex" to start a label. Demo measure names keep their source spelling.

terms.definition: Capex plus opex over the life of an alternative.
terms.notes: Spell it out (rule 8.34).

terms.definition: A dated point in an alternative's schedule.
A step in an investment's life cycle, such as Concept or Approved.
terms.notes: Stage names as entered.

terms.definition: An approval point between stages.
terms.notes: "Approved at every gate" (rule 14.12).

terms.definition: The ordered people who approve an investment or framework.
Agree that the item can move on.
Status: an approver sent the item back to its author to revise.
terms.notes: The send-back pair (decided Nov 26): the asker's button "Request revisions", their snackbar "Revisions requested — sent back to {name}", the status everyone sees "Needs revision". A status that asks for action may start with "Needs" (rule 8.52).

terms.definition: The chance and impact of an unwanted event, such as an asset failure.
The risk left after an investment is done.
The list of identified risks and their scores.
A physical thing the organization owns and maintains, such as a transformer or pole.
terms.notes: Asset names as entered ("Transformer T-118").

terms.definition: How healthy an asset is today, on the organization's scale.
The sources that support a score, a recommendation or Cooper's answer.
terms.notes: "Supporting evidence" in CooperMessage (rule 8.59).

terms.definition: How sure Cooper or the system is about an inference: High, Medium or Low.
The IFS Copperleaf assistant.
terms.notes: Always capitalised. "I" only for its own actions and limits; third person outside the chat ("Suggested by Cooper").

terms.definition: The people who use Copperleaf, when UI text talks about others ("People with access"); the reader is "you".
terms.notes: Decided Nov 26. "User" stays fine in code and prop names; the approval column is "Person".

terms.definition: The group a chart folds its smallest series or slices into.
terms.notes: Grey --color-data-viz-other (rules 10.1, 10.7).

terms.definition: A missing data point in a chart tooltip. Only there; empty states follow rules 8.22 and 8.51.
terms.notes: Rule 10.10.

terms.definition: A person working on a record with you.
The person responsible for a record.
terms.notes: Role names are labels in sentence case ("Portfolio owner"), lowercase mid-sentence (rule 8.33).

verbs.for: putting an existing or new item into a container ("Add model")
taking out of a group, without deleting ("Remove collaborator")
making a copy in the same place ("Duplicate scenario")
keeping edits; the FormCard fallback label
applying filters or a setting without leaving
avoid: Apply (for a Cooper suggestion: name the change)

verbs.for: approver decisions; "Request revisions" sends the item back to its author
verbs.notes: After "Request revisions" the status is "Needs revision" and the snackbar "Revisions requested — sent back to {name}".

verbs.for: files out of or into the product ("Export plan (CSV)")
moving a file as a file
a decision between options, in instructions
repeating a failed load or action

banned.avoid: please, sorry (more than once, or when nothing failed), oops
banned.use: the fact and the next step

banned.avoid: seamless, powerful, robust, magic, smart, AI-powered, revolutionary
click here, here, read more, learn more (alone)
invalid, illegal, failed, fatal, abort, error (alone)
banned.use: say what's wrong ("Enter a date after Jan 1, 2027")
verb + object ("Send for approval"); "Save" in a form

banned.avoid: Apply, Do it (on a Cooper suggestion)
banned.use: the change, named in full ("Defer 3 investments")

banned.avoid: No data, No data found, Nothing here, No results found
banned.use: the rule 8.22 heading for the cause ("No results for “WDRM-2”", "No matches for these filters")
"Not enough data yet" + when it will appear
people ("People with access"), you, or the person's name

banned.avoid: As an AI…, I think, I feel, I'd love to, Great question

banned.use: for example, that is, the full list, compared with

banned.avoid: straight quotes and apostrophes (" ' ) in UI strings
log in, login, log out, sign on
Request more information, Request more info, Request changes
Revisions required, Revision required, Revision requested, Changes requested (as a status)

banned.use: constraint, or the limit's own name
sentence case (rule 2.9), no emoji, a full stop
